To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the accumulation of NA in the proximal segment of the nerve is arrested after 48 hr, 2) this arrest is not due to a decrease in the rate of synthesis, 3) it is not due to an increase in rate of transport, 4) it is not caused by a failure in transport of the amine storage granule, and 5) it is probably caused by a failure to form new granules in the distal segment.
the accumulation of NA proximal to the ligation of a sciatic nerve is due to a block of axonal transport.
axotomy and axonal crush cause a rapid and transient increase in the rate of synthesis of amine storage vesicles in the proximal stump of rat sciatic nerve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and transport in axons of a specific class of organelles, the amine storage granule.
the effect of different types, and degrees of axonal injury, on the transport of amine granules in the peripheral nervous system.
the effect of axonal damage on the synthesis and axonal transport of the amine storage granule in the rat sciatic nerve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of NA in axons of peripheral nerves is not impaired in the presence of a crush or a ligature, but that the transport of the NA is arrested by the operation.

in the case of the sciatic nerve of the rat, a crush lesion of a few days duration is a better model for the study of the regeneration of peripheral nerves than a cut or ligature, since in the former case the nerve is less damaged and the axons are less likely to degenerate.
the accumulation of NA in proximal segments of crushed nerves is not due to the accumulation of newly synthesized NA, but to the accumulation of NA which is already in the nerve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in all types of axonal injury studied, the accumulation of amine storage material proximal to the injury site ceases to increase after 48 hr, and the amine storage granule synthesis is not increased in the distal stump.

there is no evidence that the accumulation of nor-adrenaline in the proximal stump after crush or ligation of a sciatic nerve of the rat is dependent on a synthesis and/or transport of amine-storage granules in the proximal part of the nerve, and that the accumulation of NA in the proximal portion of the nerve is not a result of a synthesis and transport of newly synthesized NA in the proximally located axons.
the synthesis of NA in the proximal stump after crushing is not impaired.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis and axonal transport of the amine storage granule proteins are differentially affected by axonal injury.
the axonal injury that results from a crush is more severe than the injury that results from an axotomy or a ligation.
axonal transport of amine granules is severely affected by axonal trauma and that the effect depends on the type of trauma.
